previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest tightness, bilateral leg edema, and a 10-pound weight gain over one week, initially raising concern for cardiac ischemia. Evaluation revealed normal cardiac enzymes and EKG, with symptoms attributed to anxiety and depression. She was found to have a UTI caused by ESBL-producing E. coli, prompting IV meropenem therapy. Due to her history of ESBL-related sepsis, a 10-day antibiotic course was planned, requiring a PICC line for outpatient ertapenem. The PICC was placed on the morning of discharge after a delay. Her edema, likely exacerbated by high salt intake and obstructive sleep apnea, improved significantly with IV and oral furosemide, resulting in a 25-pound weight loss. A DVT was ruled out, and her subtherapeutic INR at discharge was attributed to antibiotic-warfarin interaction. Chronic conditions including HIV, hepatitis C, and cirrhosis were stable. Follow-up was arranged for pulmonary (CPAP adjustment), orthopedics (shoulder pain), psychiatry, and a CT chest for a persistent RUL opacity.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ with PMH significant for HIV (last CD4 792, VL 
undetectable), Hepatitis C, diastolic CHF (preserved EF) who 
presents with B/L extremity edema, dyspnea, and urinary 
incontinence with dysuria with CXR showing volume overload in 
the setting of known diastolic dysfunction.
.
# DYSPNEA - patient presented with 2-days of shortness of 
breath/dyspnea; known diastolic dysfunction with preserved EF 
thought to be attributed to her obstructive sleep apnea; last 2D 
echo LVEF > 55%, patient noted failure to comply with Lasix 
regimen and presented with bilateral ___ edema. She likely has 
acute on chronic CHF exacerbation with evidence of volume 
overload. Pulmonary embolus was suspected in the setting of 
sub-therapeutic INR 1.8 along with given history of DVT. Her OSA 
was likely contributing to dyspnea (failure to comply with 
CPAP). She had a lung/V-Q scan that demonstrated a moderately 
low likelihood of PE. A repeat 2D echo (___) showing a 
preserved EF with mild RV hypokinesis. She was aggressively 
diuresed with Lasix 40 mg IV BID and then transitioned to Lasix 
40 mg PO daily on discharge. This had excellent effect on her 
volume overload and she diuresed appropriately. Daily weights 
were performed and on admission she was 380 lbs. She was also 
placed on a salt restriction and was noted diurese roughly 2L 
daily with Lasix. A Foley catheter was placed at the time of 
admission and was removed on discharge, at which time she was 
able to void without difficulty.
.
# BILATERAL LOWER EXTREMITY EDEMA - This appeared similar to 
previous episodes in which she was responsive to Lasix. Her 
edema was likely realted to diastolic dysfunction and RHF 
etiology. She was aggressively diuresed with Lasix and this 
improved markedly.
.
# ATYPICAL CHEST PAIN - She presented with vague, atypical chest 
pain which was substernal of stabbing quality which she has 
experienced previously; a cardiac cath in ___ was unrevealing; 
her Troponin in the ED was < 0.01 and previous cardiac work-up's 
were unrevealing; her EKG was stable on admission and two sets 
of troponins were negative on serially examination
.
# URINARY INCONTINENCE/UTI - The patient had a recent admission 
demonstrating ESBL UTI treated with a 6-day course of Ertapenem 
IV with PICC line which had since been removed; she now returned 
with 4-days of dysuria and a positive U/A, which speciated 
E.coli that was again a similar organism. She was started on PO 
Bactrim which was to continue for 7-days given this complicated 
infection. Sensitivities revealed Bactrim was appopriate.
.
# HIV INFECTION - Her last CD4 was 792, and her VL was < 48 
copies; she was continued on her home HAART regimen while an 
inpatient
.
# HEPATITIS B/C - Her last VL was 733,000 IU (prior treatment 
with INF resulted in poor suppression of VL); has history of 
mild ___ f/u as outpatient with Hepatology 
regarding possible further treatments.
.
# HISTORY OF DVT - She has a history of DVT following ORIF of 
proximal tibia fracture in ___ she has been on Coumadin ___ 
mg PO daily, and will be continued on 5 mg PO Coumadin on 
discharge; her INR was found to be subtherapeutic on admission 
and once coumadin was resumed this was no issue. She was 
evaluated with a lung scan for pulmonary embolus and this scan 
was reassuring. She was maintained on HSQ until her INR was 
again therapeutic, although she refused this medication.
.
# RIGHT SHOULDER PAIN - She has a history of RUE shoulder 
discomfort since falling 1-week prior to a previous admission. 
She had evaluation with plain films that revealed no evidence of 
fracture or screw/plate malalignment. Her ROM was intact and a 
lidoderm patch was offered for supplemental treatment. She can 
continue to follow-up as an outpatient regarding this issue.
.
